question: A can lay railway track between two given stations in 18 days and B can do the same job in 10 days. With the help of C, they did the job in 4 days only. Then, C alone can do the job in
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(18, 10, 4) = 180 units.

Efficiency of A = 180 ÷ 18 = 10, B = 180 ÷ 10 = 18.

Efficiency of A + B + C = 180 ÷ 4 = 45.

Efficiency of C = 45 − (10 + 18) = 17.

Time for C alone = 180 ÷ 17 = 10¹⁰/₁₇ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10¹⁰/₁₇ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 18 days

Time taken by B = 10 days

Time taken by A, B, and C together = 4 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time Taken

⇒ Total efficiency of A, B, and C = 45 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of A = 10 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = 18 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = Total efficiency − (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 45 − (10 + 18)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 45 − 28 = 17 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 180 ÷ 17 = 10¹⁰/₁₇ days

**∴ The correct answer is 10¹⁰/₁₇ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If people work for the exact same number of days, their wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The underlying concept is identical to Time & Work. However, a pipe that empties the tank (outlet pipe) is considered to be doing negative work, subtracting from the total efficiency.

Alternate Days Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the combined work done in one complete cycle of days, then multiply the cycles until the total work is nearly completed before finding remaining days.
